teaser.text: Republic Services is a company that turns a messy physical problem—discarded material—into a chain of paid services. It collects waste, moves it, recovers what it can, and charges for the work and facilities that handle the rest.

stock.title: Republic Services stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Republic Services stock forecast: weighted scenarios, cash generation, risks and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast sees $229.93 in October 2027 and $249.26 in October 2029, including dividends. It hinges on pricing and acquisitions offsetting weak volume.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Republic Services makes money, how it compares with rivals, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could Republic Services shares go?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast sees little near-term upside, followed by a modest return if Republic delivers the base case. The weighted price is $229.93 in October 2027, a 0% return including dividends. It reaches $238.54 in October 2028, a 5% return, and $249.26 in October 2029, an 11% return. The 2029 range is wide: $161.35 in the bear case to $362.54 in the bull case, against today’s $231.54.
The probabilities are bear 30%, base 55% and bull 15%.

blocks.heading: What could go right or wrong for Republic Services?

paragraphs.text: The bear path uses $5,390 million of October 2027 EBITDA, then $5,469 million and $5,619 million. Weak construction, residential contract exits and project-sensitive Environmental Solutions outweigh pricing. The bull path uses $5,904 million, then $6,475 million and $7,075 million, assuming volume recovery, productivity, integration and polymer operations improve.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Republic Services?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash left after selected operating investments, not after every obligation. Republic must replace trucks, build landfill cells, meet environmental requirements, service debt, pay dividends, and fund acquisitions. Enterprise value adds debt to the value assigned by shareholders, less cash, so it measures the operating business before lenders are paid.

blocks.heading: How much does Republic Services pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises to $2.725 per share in October 2027. It reaches $2.905 in 2028 and $3.085 in 2029. The assumed quarterly increase is close to the latest raise, while annual dividends rose from $1.77 in 2021 to $2.41 in 2025. The bear pauses first and reaches $2.78. The bull assumes larger raises and reaches $3.13.

blocks.heading: Is Republic Services' dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The basic free-cash-flow test subtracts property and equipment spending from operating cash. That spending includes maintenance and growth projects, such as landfill cells and recycling facilities, so the statement does not reveal perfectly which dollars are optional. Subtracting stock pay gives a stricter owner-focused measure because stock compensation can dilute shareholders even when it uses no current cash.

Adjusted free cash flow is Republic’s customized version of that calculation. It may add back selected restructuring payments or recoveries, but it still excludes debt service and dividends. It is useful for comparison, not the same as cash freely available to owners.

blocks.heading: What could change Republic Services' dividend?

paragraphs.text: The bear view would gain force in 2027–2028 if construction and industrial weakness kept volume and revenue growth falling. Through 2029, customer churn after price increases, weaker Environmental Solutions results and higher debt would reduce EBITDA, buybacks and the valuation multiple.

The base view would strengthen if pricing and acquired businesses delivered modest growth, volumes improved gradually and route productivity protected margins. Dividends and buybacks would continue, but capital spending and acquisitions would still absorb cash.

blocks.heading: What has Republic Services guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: For the year ending December 2026, management guides to revenue of **$17,200–$17,300 million**, adjusted diluted EPS of **$7.23–$7.28**, and adjusted free cash flow of **$2,540–$2,575 million**. “Adjusted” means Republic excludes specified costs from the measure, so the exclusions matter when those costs recur.

blocks.heading: Has Republic Services kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The 2025 scorecard shows how the system works. Adjusted earnings per share came just below its annual target, while free cash flow came above target. Before the sustainability adjustment, that produced a potential annual incentive of 94.29% of target. The committee then reduced incentives by 2.5 percentage points after reviewing safety, talent, climate and customer measures. Republic also exceeded its full-year adjusted earnings-per-share and free-cash-flow guidance, though that is not the same as hitting every compensation target.

blocks.heading: What have Republic Services results looked like over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was $4.430 billion in Q2 2026, compared with $4.235 billion in Q2 2025. Gross margin was 42.1%, and operating income was $901 million. Net income was $566 million, diluted EPS was $1.84, and free cash flow was $761 million.

blocks.heading: What should Republic Services watch in the next release?

paragraphs.text: The company is scheduled to report Q3 2026 results after market close on October 29, followed by a conference call. Management expects the comparison with unusually high prior-year landfill volumes to weigh on Q3. Acquisition integration costs are also expected to be concentrated in Q3 and Q4.
The next results should be judged against volume, pricing and integration costs, while West Lake will remain unresolved until the cleanup plan and responsibility become clearer.
